answers.answer: Starting hands are 4 cards each for 2 players, 3 each for 3 players, and 2 each for 4 players. Remove and set aside all Epidemic cards before shuffling and dealing the remaining City and Event cards. Place each player's matching colored pawn in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Remove Epidemic cards and set aside”; starting-card table; matching pawns in Atlanta.

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2 space. Flip 3 Infection cards and place 3 matching-color cubes on each named city; flip 3 more and place 2 cubes on each; flip 3 more and place 1 cube on each. Put all 9 revealed cards face up on the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining Infection cards form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, “Infect initial cities”.

answers.answer: Choose 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic; remove unused Epidemics from the game. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles, as equal in size as possible. Shuffle one Epidemic into each pile, keeping it face down, then stack the piles to form the Player Deck with smaller piles on the bottom. The summary does not say how to resolve an equal-size tie in pile ordering.
answers.evidence: Setup, “Prepare the Player Deck”: “equal in number to the Epidemic cards used and as equal in size as possible”; “placing smaller piles on the bottom.”

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions, repeating actions if desired (each repetition costs another action), and you may stop early. Any cards discarded to pay action costs go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve any Epidemics first, and discard cards or play Events until within the 7-card limit; next infect cities by flipping cards equal to the current infection rate. After all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions: up to 4; cards to Player Discard Pile; phases in order; play passes left.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry: move to a city connected by a white line, with no card cost. Direct Flight: discard the City card naming the destination to move there. Charter Flight: discard the City card matching your current city to move to any city. Shuttle Flight: from a city with a research station, move to any other city with a research station, with no card cost stated. White lines going off one edge wrap to the other edge (the summary gives Sydney–Los Angeles as an example).
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table; Special Rules: “Board wrapping”.

answers.answer: Normally, discard the City card matching your current city, take a research station from the supply, and place it in your current city. If all 6 stations are already built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than 6, set the extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Other Actions, “Build a Research Station”; Special Rules, “Research station limit” and extras.

answers.answer: A non-Medic's Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen cured color in that city, returning them to the cube supply. A separate Treat Disease action is needed for each different color. An uncured color loses only 1 cube per Treat Disease action. The summary does not give a separate method for clearing the remaining cubes other than taking further Treat Disease actions; cubes return to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: “If that disease is cured, return all cubes of that one color”; “Treat each different color with a separate action”; removed cubes return to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the same disease color (4 if you are the Scientist) and move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator; the station city's color need not match the disease. Existing cubes remain, and the cured disease can still infect in infections and Epidemics until eradicated. If there are no cubes of that color on the board when the cure is discovered, immediately eradicate it and flip its marker.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure.

answers.answer: Give another player in the same city the City card matching that city, or take that matching card from them; both players must agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they must immediately discard or play an Event card until within the limit (the general hand-limit sequence prioritizes resolving any Epidemics just drawn, then reducing the hand).
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge; Hand Limit: applies immediately after Share Knowledge.

answers.answer: When sharing, the Researcher may give any City card from the Researcher's hand to a player in the same city, not only the matching city card. This can happen on either player's turn. The exception only transfers a card from the Researcher's hand; another player cannot use it to give the Researcher an arbitrary nonmatching City card.
answers.evidence: Roles, Researcher; Special Rules, “Researcher exception”.

answers.answer: After actions, draw 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the game ends and the players lose; do not reshuffle the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards.

answers.answer: Resolve the Epidemic in order: (1) advance the Infection Rate marker 1 space; (2) draw the bottom Infection card, place cubes of its color in its city up to a total of 3—since the city already has 2, add 1 cube—and an outbreak occurs because it already had cubes of that color; discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile; (3) reshuffle only the Infection Discard Pile and put it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the Epidemic card from the game. Do not draw a replacement Player card. The summary says a city with existing cubes receives only enough to reach 3, then an outbreak occurs; it does not specify the full outbreak resolution in this Epidemic-specific paragraph, but the outbreak rules apply.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards steps 1–3 and no replacement; outbreak rule.

answers.answer: After 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics, respectively, flip 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4 Infection cards during the Infect Cities phase.
answers.evidence: Infection Rate Track and Player Reference infection-rate table.

answers.answer: Resolve the first Epidemic completely through Increase, Infect, and Intensify, then resolve the second through all three steps. Events may be played between the two Epidemics. Reduce an over-limit hand only after first resolving any Epidemic cards just drawn; then discard cards or play Events until at most 7.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: two drawn at once resolved in sequence, Events between; Hand Limit steps 1–2.

answers.answer: Flip Infection cards from the top of the Infection Deck, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For each card, place 1 matching-color cube in the named city if the disease is not eradicated; if eradicated, place none. A cured but not eradicated disease still places a cube normally. If the city already has 3 cubes of that color, place no fourth cube and cause an outbreak. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities; Cure Procedure: cured disease can still infect until eradication.

answers.answer: When a city outbreaks, move the Outbreaks marker forward 1 space, then place 1 cube of that color in every connected city. If a connected city already has 3 cubes of that color, it has a chain-reaction outbreak after the current outbreak resolves, causing another marker advance and spread. During chain reactions, do not add cubes to cities that already had an outbreak during resolution of that Infection card; therefore spread does not return into the first outbreak city. A city may hold multiple colors, up to 3 cubes of each color, rather than sharing one 3-cube cap across colors.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks steps 1–4; city cap: “up to 3 of each”.

answers.answer: No. Airlift cannot be played between drawing an Infection card and resolving that card, so it cannot move the Quarantine Specialist after the card is drawn to prevent that outbreak. Event cards may be played at any time except between drawing and resolving a card; before the next Infection card is drawn, the Event may be played. The player who plays Airlift chooses its use. It costs no action; discard it to the Player Discard Pile after play.
answers.evidence: Event Cards timing, chooser and discard; Airlift effect; “Cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card.”

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes 1 Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Role card. Only 1 Event can be stored, and it does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove that Event from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Roles, Contingency Planner.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may either move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if it were the Dispatcher's own; the owner must agree when moving another player's pawn. For Direct or Charter Flights while directing another pawn, the Dispatcher discards cards from the Dispatcher's own hand; for a Charter Flight, the card matches the moved pawn's departure city. The Dispatcher may move another pawn but cannot make it Treat Disease or perform other nonmovement actions. The Dispatcher cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.
answers.evidence: Roles, Dispatcher.

answers.answer: Players win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; diseases need not be eradicated and cubes may remain on the board. They lose if the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (the 8th outbreak), if they cannot place the required number of disease cubes of a needed color (during an Epidemic, outbreak, or infection), or if a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after actions. The cube-supply loss occurs immediately when the required cubes cannot be placed.
answers.evidence: Victory; Defeat; Special Rules, “Cube supply check.”

answers.answer: Place the board within reach and put the 6 research stations and disease cubes, separated by color, nearby. Put 1 research station in Atlanta and the Outbreaks marker on 0. Place the 4 Cure markers vial-side up near the Discovered Cure Indicators. Give each player a Reference card; shuffle the Role cards and deal 1 face up to each player, place matching-color pawns in Atlanta, and remove unused Role cards and pawns. The player with the highest-population City card goes first.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–5 and 9.

answers.answer: Teammates may offer advice, but the active player decides their actions. In Introductory games, play with cards face up for all to see. In Standard and Heroic, keep hands private by default; experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may examine either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Special Rules, “Introductory game.”

answers.answer: Removing the last cube of a disease before it is cured does not eradicate it or change anything. Removing the last cube of a cured disease eradicates it; flip its cure marker to the eradication side. After eradication, no new cubes of that disease are placed during normal infections or Epidemics.
answers.evidence: Eradication.

answers.answer: Increase the Infection Rate marker 1 space, then draw the bottom Infection card. Since the unprotected city has zero cubes of that non-eradicated color, place 3 cubes there. There is no outbreak simply for reaching 3: an outbreak happens if the city already has 3 and would receive a fourth (or the Epidemic rule's city already has cubes and reaches 3). Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify; then reshuffle only that discard pile and place it on top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards steps 1–3; outbreaks occur when 3 cubes already present and a further placement is needed.

answers.answer: Increase still occurs. The bottom Infection card is drawn, but because its disease is eradicated, no cubes are placed. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile, then Intensify by reshuffling only that discard pile and placing it on top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards; Infecting Cities: eradicated disease gets no cube.

answers.answer: Resolve each Epidemic fully in sequence. After the first Intensify empties the Infection Discard Pile, the second Epidemic draws its bottom Infection card and discards it to that pile; the second Intensify therefore shuffles only that one card and puts it on top. The second Epidemic city, initially at zero cubes, gets 3 matching cubes. When normal Infection draws that city, it is drawn first; it causes an outbreak because that city already has 3 cubes, unless an Event, eradication, or role protection prevents it.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards, two-Epidemic special case.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs 4 City cards of the same color instead of 5 to discover a cure. The action still requires being at any research station; the station city's color need not match the disease color.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure; Scientist role.

answers.answer: As an action, the Operations Expert builds a research station in the city the Expert currently occupies. No City card is needed, used, or discarded.
answers.evidence: Roles, Operations Expert.

answers.answer: Once per turn, as an action, the Operations Expert may move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card. The discarded card need not match the departure city or destination; the summary specifies any City card. It is an action and may be used once per turn.
answers.evidence: Roles, Operations Expert: “Once per turn as an action: move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card.”

answers.answer: A Medic's Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen color from the city, even when that disease is uncured. The action does not remove multiple colors at once; choose one color.
answers.evidence: Roles, Medic: Treat Disease removes all cubes of one color.

answers.answer: When the cure is discovered, if the Medic is already in a city with cubes of that color, remove those cubes there immediately. Later, when another player moves the Medic into another city with cubes of the cured color via Dispatcher or Airlift, automatically remove all cubes of that color from the Medic's city upon entering, including on another player's turn. This automatic removal costs no action.
answers.evidence: Roles, Medic: immediate removal upon cure; Dispatcher or Airlift entry triggers automatic removal.

answers.answer: The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the city the Medic occupies. This protection does not extend to adjacent cities and does not cover uncured diseases.
answers.evidence: Roles, Medic.

answers.answer: The Quarantine Specialist prevents disease-cube placement and outbreaks of every disease color in the Specialist's current city and all cities connected to it. The ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.
answers.evidence: Roles, Quarantine Specialist.

answers.answer: Resilient Population removes any 1 card in the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between the Infect and Intensify steps of an Epidemic, so it can remove the Infection card just discarded during that Epidemic before Intensify shuffles the pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Resilient Population effect and timing.

answers.answer: One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step, so no Infection cards are flipped for that step. It does not skip an Epidemic's Infect step.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: One Quiet Night.

answers.answer: Airlift moves any 1 pawn to any city. If it is another player's pawn, get that player's permission.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Airlift.

answers.answer: Only Player cards count toward the 7-card limit. Role and Reference cards do not count; an Event stored on the Contingency Planner's Role card also does not count. For a hand of 9 Player cards, discard cards or play Events until at most 7 remain (after first resolving any Epidemics just drawn, if applicable).
answers.evidence: Hand Limit; Contingency Planner role; hand-limit order.

answers.answer: Government Grant places a research station in any city, regardless of where the player is, with no City card discard needed.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Government Grant.

answers.answer: Forecast lets you draw, view, and rearrange the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, then put those cards back on top of that deck.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Forecast.
